subject: Production: Oxford Health private cluster - decode errors, concurrency spike and latency
messages:
From: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@oxfordhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: devops@oxfordhealth.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden spike in decode errors and queue backlog on our private deployment

Hi David / Laura,

We're seeing a production impact across our private VPC cluster starting ~08:45 PDT: p95 latency for API calls has doubled from ~180ms to ~380ms, and since 09:00 we've observed frequent decode errors (502/504 style) for requests that previously succeeded. Throughput dropped by ~25% as the queue backlog grows. It looks like concurrency is pegged on a few nodes and requests are piling up behind a small set of hot shards.

Impact: customer-facing inference flows are timing out, two of our clinical partners reported delayed responses on triage checks. This is high priority for us.

I've attached a short log extract and a grafana snapshot (cluster-metrics-20270517.png) showing the p95 and node QPS.

Can you triage? We can join a call immediately. If this needs exec attention we will loop in procurement/ops, but our CTO is monitoring.

Attachments: oxford_error_snippet.log (text), cluster-metrics-20270517.png (png)

Thanks,
Sarah Miller
VP Product, Oxford Health
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@oxfordhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in decode errors and queue backlog on our private deployment

Thanks for the heads up, Sarah — sorry about the disruption. Laura and our on-call infra team are taking this as P0.

Immediate plan:
- Laura, can you surface a quick triage and whether this is config, kernel mismatch, or workload-driven?
- We'll open a transient capacity bump on the cluster (reserve +1 node) while we confirm the root cause.
- Schedule: quick sync in 15 minutes? I'm available now.

Sarah — if you can join a short bridge that would help, we'll bring the metrics and logs.

— David
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@oxfordhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in decode errors and queue backlog on our private deployment

On Mon, May 17, 2027 at 09:28 AM David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the heads up, Sarah — sorry about the disruption. Laura and our on-call infra team are taking this as P0.

We ran a short triage and pulled the following immediate signals: 
- p95 token decode latency doubled; decode error rate (502/504) increased selectively on 3 nodes (node IDs attached in oxford_error_snippet.log).
- The hot nodes show repeated KV cache evictions when sequence length distribution spikes; most traffic is hitting the same model shard set and causing contention on the runtime's KV layer.
- Model kernel mappings look correct, but we are observing elevated contention in the decoder path (likely workload pattern: sudden high-concurrency small prompt bursts).

Short-term mitigation proposed (can be enacted immediately):
1) Temporary capacity bump: +2 replica nodes in the VPC for the next 6 hours (auto-reduce after window).
2) Apply a conservative KV cache retention tweak on the affected nodes (increase local cache size by 20%) and restart the runtime process to force fresh cache warm.
3) Route a portion (~30%) of traffic to the compatible lowered-quant model variant to reduce decode latency while preserving response quality.

I've attached cluster metrics and a short error snippet. quick notes in oxford_error_snippet.log show stack traces and node identifiers. This approach should reduce p95 and clear backlog in 20–30 minutes after node bump + cache change.

Karthik — I'm adding you because the proposed plan touches reserved capacity limits and would need an SLA exception for the temporary bump.

Laura Bennett
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: cluster-metrics-20270517.png, oxford_error_snippet.log
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@oxfordhealth.com>, procurement@oxfordhealth.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in decode errors and queue backlog on our private deployment

Looping in leadership and ops for an exec decision.

Summary for execs: Oxford Health private VPC is experiencing a workload-driven concurrency spike that is causing KV cache thrashing on three nodes, resulting in elevated p95 latency and decode errors. Laura's triage indicates the root cause is workload-pattern (high-frequency small requests) leading to hot-shard contention.

Proposal (requires approval):
- Immediate: grant SLA exception to add +2 reserved nodes for 6 hours (estimated incremental cost: $2.1k for the window) and trigger Laura's KV retention change.
- Medium: schedule a 2-week tuning engagement (model variant recommendation + runtime kernel profiling + tailored batching) — propose a funded services engagement (scope and SOW to follow).

Risk/impact: If we do not act quickly, Oxford will see ongoing degraded customer experience and potential churn risk with clinical partners. Acting reduces immediate customer impact and buys us time to implement a robust tuning plan.

Decision needed: Approve the one-time capacity bump and authorize services scoping with Oxford.

— Karthik Iyer
VP Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@oxfordhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, procurement@oxfordhealth.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 18:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Action plan: capacity bump + hotfix rollout and next steps

Sarah — following internal approvals, here's the agreed action plan and timeline: 
1) Today 18:15 PDT: transient +2 node capacity bump in Oxford's VPC (ops to start now). Expected backlog drain within 20–30 minutes.
2) 18:30 PDT: Laura will apply the KV retention tweak and restart runtime on affected nodes (short ~45s rolling restarts).
3) 19:00 PDT: Route 30% traffic to the compatible quant variant for 4 hours as fallback. We'll monitor p95 and error rate.
4) By EOD Fri: Karthik to send SOW for a 2-week tuning engagement (kernel profiling, quantization recommendations, routing policy adjustments).

Please confirm you accept the short maintenance window. We'll keep the status channel updated and share Grafana links.

Attachments: proposed-hotfix-checklist.pdf

Thanks for your patience — we'll remain on the bridge until metrics are stable.

— David
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
